title: Bittensor Daily News: November 24, 2026

updates.headline: SN28 SayGM connects Bijou agents through a shared AI balance
updates.summary:
SN28 SayGM's November 23 case study identifies Bijou as the first third-party application to ship Sign in with SayGM. Bijou's own website also lists the connection. It lets users connect an AI provider without manually creating and pasting an API key.

The documented sign-in flow creates an application-specific key, supports a monthly spending limit and lets the user revoke access. SayGM says Bijou users can choose among more than 70 models using one provider balance. This is a concrete application integration, not evidence that 70 model developers have entered partnerships with the subnet.

There is a billing-description discrepancy: the case study says Bijou retired its own AI credit, while Bijou's current pricing page still lists included AI usage and top-ups alongside provider connections. We therefore confirm the integration without claiming every Bijou plan has eliminated its own usage allowance. Customer uptake and revenue from the integration were not independently measured.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a named application has implemented a documented sign-in and billing connection, beyond a routine catalog addition. Five is not supported by the presently established deployment scope.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: a named application has implemented a documented sign-in and billing connection, beyond a routine catalog addition. Five is not supported by the presently established deployment scope.
ratingAssessment.evidence: SayGM case study, November 23; Bijou product and pricing page
ratingAssessment.scope: SayGM case study and Bijou counterparty website.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Pricing descriptions differ; no measured adoption total asserted.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Four stars: a named application has implemented a documented sign-in and billing connection, beyond a routine catalog addition. Five is not supported by the presently established deployment scope.

updates.headline: SN55 NIOME outlines expansion into genetic-treatment design and evaluation
updates.summary:
In a November 18 roadmap now reviewed as a dated catch-up, SN55 NIOME describes its role in Genomes.io's proposed genetic-medicine development engine. The subnet currently supplies synthetic genomic modeling; the team plans to add treatment-design and candidate-evaluation work.

The proposed workflow connects knowledge, population modeling, design, evaluation and physical experiments. NIOME reports 10 million synthetic CRISPR experiments as groundwork. These are simulations, not 10 million clinical experiments or demonstrated patient treatments.

The team's goal is to reduce a development program from roughly four years and $25 million to one year and $2.5 million. Those figures are targets, not achieved savings. The roadmap does not establish completed clinical validation or a newly signed external customer contract. Yesterday's separate revenue disclosure remains covered in the November 23 edition.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: a substantive expansion of the subnet's proposed scientific work deserves more than routine roadmap coverage. Five is not supported by unachieved development targets or clinical outcomes.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: a substantive expansion of the subnet's proposed scientific work deserves more than routine roadmap coverage. Five is not supported by unachieved development targets or clinical outcomes.
ratingAssessment.scope: Original NIOME article, November 18; catch-up after November 23 secondary coverage.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Design/evaluation expansion and cost/time gains remain plans; clinical efficacy not established.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Four stars: a substantive expansion of the subnet's proposed scientific work deserves more than routine roadmap coverage. Five is not supported by unachieved development targets or clinical outcomes.

updates.headline: SN64 Chutes documents Hermes setup and its routing requirements
updates.summary:
In a November 23 announcement, SN64 Chutes linked its Hermes setup guide. The guide explains how to connect the agent through a named OpenAI-compatible provider, keep the API key in the environment and select a model from the live catalog. This is setup guidance, not a strategic-partnership announcement.

The practical distinction is routing setup: a concrete model ID can be used immediately, while aliases such as default:latency require a saved Model Routing pool. The guide includes troubleshooting for absent pools and missing authentication. We verified the public instructions, not an installed Hermes session or a paid inference request.
updates.ratingReason: Two stars: useful configuration guidance and a concrete setup caveat, but not a new product or partnership warranting three or four.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Two stars: useful configuration guidance and a concrete setup caveat, but not a new product or partnership warranting three or four.
ratingAssessment.scope: Original November 23 Chutes post and full public Hermes guide.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Two stars: useful configuration guidance and a concrete setup caveat, but not a new product or partnership warranting three or four.

updates.headline: SN65 TPN reports Gratis usage and 305 paid Bench runs
updates.summary:
SN65 True Performance Network reported on November 24 that Gratis had processed more than three million requests from over 9,300 unique users in its first 22 days. The team separately reported 390 unique Bench users and 305 paid runs. Requests, users and paid runs measure different things; the post supplies no revenue total.

Bench offers model optimization and evaluation services, including quantization, benchmarking, conversion and comparison. The team also scheduled Gratis's Product Hunt launch for November 25 at 09:00 CET, which is 03:00 Eastern. That launch remains upcoming.

TPN-009 is underway with a target of fitting Gemma 4 26B-A4B below 14 GiB. This is the competition target, not a completed winning result. Usage figures are attributed to TPN and were not independently audited.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: quantified usage and paid-run disclosures are useful operating evidence beyond promotion. Four is not established by these self-reported totals and a scheduled listing alone; competition details retain the three-star cap.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Three stars: quantified usage and paid-run disclosures are useful operating evidence beyond promotion. Four is not established by these self-reported totals and a scheduled listing alone; competition details retain the three-star cap.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Metrics unaudited; upcoming listing and competition outcome not yet completed.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Three stars: quantified usage and paid-run disclosures are useful operating evidence beyond promotion. Four is not established by these self-reported totals and a scheduled listing alone; competition details retain the three-star cap.

updates.headline: SN79 MVTRX doubles its simulated order-book capacity to 256
updates.summary:
SN79 MVTRX reported on November 24 that it expanded simulation capacity during November from 128 to 256 order books. The new total is split across three markets: 128 books in one and 64 in each of the other two.

The team says the expanded environments let AI agents interact with orders, liquidity and changing market conditions, supporting evaluation of execution behavior as well as price predictions. This is simulation infrastructure capacity. It is not a claim that the subnet doubled live exchange trading volume, customer assets or Bittensor neuron slots. The capacity figures are team-reported rather than independently load-tested.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: doubling a defined simulation resource is a meaningful operational expansion. Four would overstate the evidence without a broader new product or demonstrated deployment consequence.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Three stars: doubling a defined simulation resource is a meaningful operational expansion. Four would overstate the evidence without a broader new product or demonstrated deployment consequence.
ratingAssessment.scope: Original MVTRX November 24 post describes work completed during November.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: No independent capacity test or live exchange-volume claim.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Three stars: doubling a defined simulation resource is a meaningful operational expansion. Four would overstate the evidence without a broader new product or demonstrated deployment consequence.

updates.headline: SN92 REAX operator adds bison-1 to Decision Models API
updates.summary:
Decision Models, the operator associated with SN92 REAX, announced bison-1 availability on November 23. Its model page offers an EU-tier, pay-per-token decision API using published Base Labs weights, with typed answers and probabilities. This is hosted model availability, not a claimed partnership with Base Labs, Baseten or Google.

The reviewed service page lists a starting input price of EUR 0.09 per million tokens with output free. It specifies BF16 serving, up to three text questions per call and one request at a time; a busy service returns a capacity-limit response that is not billed.

The public model and access documentation are verified. We did not execute a paid request, and the announcement does not establish that this third-party model is REAX's own newly trained model or quantify revenue flowing to the subnet.
updates.ratingReason: Three stars: a new model and concrete access terms extend an existing provider catalog. Four would incorrectly treat routine hosting availability as a substantive partnership or new original model.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Three stars: a new model and concrete access terms extend an existing provider catalog. Four would incorrectly treat routine hosting availability as a substantive partnership or new original model.
ratingAssessment.evidence: Decision Models announcement, November 23; bison-1 availability and API limits
ratingAssessment.scope: Original Decision Models announcement and live bison-1 service page.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Paid inference and subnet revenue attribution not verified.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Three stars: a new model and concrete access terms extend an existing provider catalog. Four would incorrectly treat routine hosting availability as a substantive partnership or new original model.

updates.headline: SN98 NeverPlayAlone opens Studio and brings agents to existing Minecraft servers
updates.summary:
SN98 NeverPlayAlone's November 24 release opens Studio to every verified account. Users can describe builds, quests, skins and other Minecraft assets, with 40 creations per day for accounts with verified email. A new Explore catalog brings worlds, agents, skins and mods together.

The update also supports bringing an existing Minecraft Java server on versions 1.21.4 or 1.21.11. Owners verify control using a code in the server description, link a Minecraft account and send agents to that server. Seven-day invite links support up to eight guests in a world, without giving guests control of its agents.

Agent 1.4.1 adds autonomous food-seeking and user-defined mob rules. The changelog also says agent hours count only while an agent is connected and able to act. These are the team's published release details; we have not conducted a paid gameplay or performance test.
updates.ratingReason: Four stars: opening creation tools and supporting existing customer servers materially extends the usable product beyond maintenance. Five is not established by this release scope alone.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: opening creation tools and supporting existing customer servers materially extends the usable product beyond maintenance. Five is not established by this release scope alone.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Gameplay and paid service delivery not independently tested; attached tour pending review.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Four stars: opening creation tools and supporting existing customer servers materially extends the usable product beyond maintenance. Five is not established by this release scope alone.

ecosystem.headline: Bittensor raises subnet capacity to 160 and widens the emission gate
ecosystem.summary:
Bittensor has increased its subnet limit from 128 to 160 and moved its emission gate from rank 32 to 48. OpenTensor announced both changes on November 23. A direct finalized-chain check this morning confirms the new settings.

The changes address different constraints. The higher limit creates room for 32 additional subnet slots; the wider gate allows more subnets to compete for meaningful emissions. Neither number means that all 160 slots are already occupied or that every subnet receives the same allocation.

At our November 24 snapshot, the chain still contained 128 non-root subnets, plus the root network. The parameter change is verified, but this report does not attribute individual price moves to it or present modeled emission gains as realized results.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Four stars: an executed network-wide capacity and allocation-policy change exceeds a routine three-star update. Five is not established without evidence of exceptional realized consequences beyond the parameter expansion.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: an executed network-wide capacity and allocation-policy change exceeds a routine three-star update. Five is not established without evidence of exceptional realized consequences beyond the parameter expansion.
ratingAssessment.evidence: OpenTensor announcement, November 23; Finalized network parameters, November 24
ratingAssessment.scope: Official announcement and finalized block 9577088 storage values.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Exact activation block and realized redistribution not established in this targeted snapshot.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Four stars: an executed network-wide capacity and allocation-policy change exceeds a routine three-star update. Five is not established without evidence of exceptional realized consequences beyond the parameter expansion.

ecosystem.headline: Runtime 494 adds commitment, delegation and basket-trading controls
ecosystem.summary:
The Subtensor runtime 494 release was published on November 23, and our finalized-chain snapshot confirms version 494 running on Finney this morning. Its release notes list burn-for-commit, per-mechanism weight delegation, configurable basket-trading controls and changes to eTAO update timing.

These are protocol tools for commitments, validator delegation and network parameter management. The release also includes a Python compatibility-floor fix and runtime-announcement changes. Release availability and the running runtime version are verified separately; the snapshot does not establish the exact upgrade activation block.

A configurable control is not evidence that every subnet has enabled it. Full intervening eTAO and burn-event reconciliation remains incomplete and is disclosed in the coverage notes.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Four stars: a deployed runtime containing new network controls exceeds routine maintenance. Five is not established by the bounded capability additions documented here.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: a deployed runtime containing new network controls exceeds routine maintenance. Five is not established by the bounded capability additions documented here.
ratingAssessment.evidence: Subtensor runtime 494 release; Finalized runtime version
ratingAssessment.scope: Official runtime release and direct finalized runtime version.

ecosystem.headline: OpenTensor launches Federation builder hubs in France, India and China
ecosystem.summary:
OpenTensor's new Federation initiative announced its first hubs in France, India and China on November 23. Each national hub is to be led by a local team and organize activities for existing Bittensor contributors and newcomers.

The announcement describes local meetups and university outreach as part of the effort to develop the builder community. Federation also reports that earlier OpenTensor and HackQuest activities reached 15 universities and more than 2,300 total attendances across 30 events. Those are organizer-reported attendances, not a count of new subnet founders or unique customers.

The launch is verified as an organizational announcement. Future events and their outcomes remain distinct from the launch itself.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Four stars: an official multi-country builder program has broader ecosystem scope than a routine meetup. Five is not established by launch announcements and prior attendance figures.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Four stars: an official multi-country builder program has broader ecosystem scope than a routine meetup. Five is not established by launch announcements and prior attendance figures.
ratingAssessment.evidence: Federation launch; National-hub operating model; Organizer-reported prior outreach
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Future event delivery and participant outcomes not established; video not fully reviewed.
ratingAssessment.adjacentRatingReason: Four stars: an official multi-country builder program has broader ecosystem scope than a routine meetup. Five is not established by launch announcements and prior attendance figures.

ecosystem.headline: TAO.com raises crosschain swap ceiling to $100,000 and reports $10 million in volume
ecosystem.summary:
TAO.com announced on November 23 that crosschain swaps can now reach $100,000 per transaction, subject to available liquidity. Its current website advertises the same limit for swaps between Ethereum USDC or ETH and Bittensor tokens, in either direction.

The team also reports $10 million in gross crosschain swap volume through TAO Intents. Gross volume is the value moved through swaps, not platform revenue, profit or net new capital entering Bittensor. The post does not specify a measurement period or a unique-user count.

We verified the published limit and product interface without connecting a wallet or executing a transaction. A displayed ceiling does not guarantee a $100,000 quote for every token or market condition.
ecosystem.ratingReason: Three stars: a higher transaction ceiling and quantified usage are meaningful operating developments. Four is not established by a limit increase and gross-volume disclosure alone.

ratingAssessment.consequence: Three stars: a higher transaction ceiling and quantified usage are meaningful operating developments. Four is not established by a limit increase and gross-volume disclosure alone.
ratingAssessment.evidence: Original provider post and current public interface.
ratingAssessment.scope: Published transaction ceiling and attributed gross-volume milestone.
ratingAssessment.uncertainty: Volume unaudited; period unspecified; no wallet connection or executed swap; video not fully reviewed.
